title: Expose the type of Corona to scripts
line: Plasma scripts can now read which shell they run in (desktop, mobile, bigscreen…) from a new shell property.
explanation: The Plasma scripting API (layout templates, update scripts, evaluateScript) exposed things like applicationVersion and screenCount but nothing about which shell package was loaded, so a script couldn't stop itself when run under Plasma Mobile or Bigscreen. The change adds a read-only shell property on AppInterface returning the corona's shell package plugin id (e.g. org.kde.plasma.desktop) and wires it into the script's global getters next to the other properties.

commits.message:
scripting: expose the shell type to scripts

Scripts had no way to tell which shell they were running in, so a
layout or update script couldn't skip itself outside Plasma Desktop.
Add a read-only shell property with the shell package's plugin id.

BUG: 515789

media.caption: Master: a script reading shell fails with "ReferenceError: shell is not defined"
With the fix: the script prints org.kde.plasma.desktop

review.text: This is a clean, minimal, idiomatic addition that exposes the active shell package plugin ID as a read-only global `shell` property in Plasma's scripting API. Naming it `shell` aligns with `plasmashell --shell` and `ShellCorona::shell()` better than internal `coronaType` jargon, and `kPackage().metadata().pluginId()` safely returns an empty string if the package is invalid. The live verification and screenshots clearly prove the before/after behavior with no regressions.
